# Limit the number of power-up slots

**Headline:** Cap the run's permanent loadout at six slots shared across power-ups *and* weapons; the first six distinct kinds taken as permanent rewards define the run, and once all six slots are full only those kinds (plus flagged always-available entries such as Extra Life and Mystery UFO) may spawn or be offered as a new permanent pick. Field pickups never consume a slot.

## Original request (verbatim)

> Currently the player can collect any number of powerups. This makes them way too powerful in late game. Limit the number of power-ups that can be collected to 6. The first 6 collected permanently (i.e. from the hull-full) become the only powerups the player can collect in that game. Once the 6 slots are full with permanent items no other powerup kind will spawn (a life powerup is an exception, there may be other exceptions later in the development cycles, so availability when full should become a flag on the powerup database entry). Until all 6 slots are full powerups will spawn as they do now.

> **Terminology:** the item text says "hull-full"; the shipped feature is the **hold-full choice** (`MineralChoiceScene`, driven by the mineral hold — GDD §4.5). This brief treats "hull-full" as "hold-full", i.e. a **permanent reward** grant. "Collected permanently" means a hold-full (or mini-boss reward) grant, never a field pickup.

## Problem statement

Players can currently collect every power-up and weapon kind in the catalogue, and every hold-full (permanent) reward can add a brand-new kind with no upper bound. By the late game a player therefore owns every permanent effect at once, which makes the ship far too powerful and flattens the difficulty curve. The run needs a bounded loadout: **six permanent slots shared across power-up and weapon kinds**. The first six distinct kinds the player takes as permanent rewards fill the slots; once all six are full, no other kind spawns or is offered as a new permanent pick, except kinds explicitly flagged as available-when-full (Extra Life and Mystery UFO today). Until the slots are full, spawning is unchanged.

## Users

- **Player (arcade run)** — wants a strong but bounded loadout, so late-game runs stay challenging and each run has a recognisable build identity; a drop on screen must still be worth catching.
- **Producer / designer** — wants the cap data-driven, with per-entry exemptions (Extra Life, Mystery UFO today; more later) needing no code change.
- **Agent / developer** — needs one shared implementation so the game and every gym behave identically (gym↔game parity).

### Example user stories

- As a player, once I have taken six permanent rewards my build is fixed for the rest of the run, so my late-game ship is strong but no longer invincible.
- As a player with six full slots, the only drops I see are the six kinds I chose (plus Extra Life and Mystery UFO), so every pickup improves something I own.
- As a designer, I can mark a catalogue entry as available-when-full, so a future exception is a data change, not a code change.
- As an operator, I can observe the identical slot rule in the gyms as in the shipped game.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Cap and shared accounting** — A single named, exported cap (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP = 6`) governs permanent ownership; occupied slots equal the count of **distinct drop kinds currently held** — power-up ids with a permanent level ≥ 1 (`PowerUpLevelStore.getLevels()` / `permanentGrants()`) **or** an active temporary (field-pickup) stack (`PowerUpLevelStore.getTempStacks()`), plus weapon drop ids with a permanent level ≥ 1 (`Player.getWeaponLevels()`) **or** an active temporary weapon stack (`Player.getTempWeaponStacks()`), i.e. one shared pool of six (producer answers 2026-10-27: Q4 = a). A slot is released when the temporary window expires (`clearTemporary` / `tickWeaponTimers`). Entries flagged `availableWhenSlotsFull` never occupy a slot (Q7 = a). The permanent cannon and the `reset` utility are never counted (they cannot be permanently granted). A unit test proves the accounting: six distinct held grants fill the pool, a repeat grant of an owned kind levels it up without consuming a new slot, a temporary stack of a new kind consumes one, and the slot frees again when the temporary window expires. Exempt entries and `reset` never occupy a slot.2. **Spawn gating at full slots** — When all six slots (permanent **or** temporary — the union) are filled, the drop-selection path (game and gyms, one shared implementation) draws only from the six held kinds plus every catalogue id flagged available-when-full (Extra Life and Mystery UFO are flagged by default) and the slot-exempt `reset` utility; every other power-up *and weapon* id is never drawn. Verified by a seeded/injected-rng unit test on the selection helper plus a `PlayScene` integration test that fills the slots and asserts a large sample of draws contains only held/exempt ids.3. **No behaviour change below the cap** — While fewer than six slots are filled, drop selection covers the full catalogue exactly as today: a regression test with a fixed rng seed produces the identical draw sequence before and after the change (power-ups and weapons alike).
4. **Choice gating at full slots** — Once the slots are full, a hold-full offer (and the mini-boss reward, which reuses the same option builder) offers **only items currently in the slots**: level-ups of permanently-owned kinds, base picks for kinds held only temporarily (taking one makes it permanent — it already occupies its slot), plus available-when-full entries (which never occupy a slot). A base entry that is neither held nor exempt is never offered, so a seventh kind can never be taken. Verified by choice-pool tests at 6 filled slots covering both power-up and weapon offers (producer answer 2026-10-27: Q6 = a, with the Q4 note: at full slots only offer items currently in the slots).5. **Data-driven exemption** — The exemption is a flag on the power-up catalogue entry (`availableWhenSlotsFull`, default `false`), not an `id === '…'` special case; Extra Life **and** Mystery UFO set it. A test asserts both are exempt, that every other catalogue entry defaults to non-exempt, and that a newly added entry is non-exempt unless it opts in. (No weapon exemption exists today; the flag stays power-up-only until a weapon needs one.)
6. **Parity and run scope** — The rule lives once in shared core code consumed by `PlayScene` and the formation gyms (guard: `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` / parity tests); slot state is run-scoped and resets on run restart (`PowerUpLevelStore.reset()` / `Player.resetWeaponLevels()`), and a temporary window's expiry also releases its slot. A parity/integration test proves the gym path and the game path consume the same gate.7. **Documentation and suite** — The GDD (§4.4 catalogue table and §4.5 hold-full choice) and `docs/BALANCING.md` document the shared six-slot cap and the exemption flag; the full project test suite passes with the change.

8. **Blocked collection at the cap with a distinct cue** — A drop whose kind is neither held, nor available-when-full, nor the slot-exempt `reset` utility is **not collectable** while the pool is full: on overlap it is not collected (no effect, no pickup cue, not removed), stays on the field, and plays a distinct **not-collectable SFX** — once per drop while it remains blocked — so the player can tell why the pickup failed (producer answer 2026-10-27: Q5 = b). When a slot frees (a temporary window expires) the same drop becomes collectable again. A test drives the shared collection seam at full slots and asserts: blocked drop kept, cue played exactly once, no effect/absorb applied; owned and exempt drops still collected; `reset` still collected; and the blocked drop is collectable after a slot frees.
## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1):** the rule must be implemented once in shared code (`src/powerups/*`, `src/scenes/core/*`) and consumed by `PlayScene` and the gyms. A gym may only diverge for a documented, disabled-feature reason — none is expected here.
- **Single counter, derived from existing stores:** no new slot counter. Slot occupancy is derived from the two permanent-grant stores (`PowerUpLevelStore`, `Player._permanentWeaponGrants`), so existing level semantics stay the only source of truth.
- **Existing level semantics unchanged:** a repeat grant of an already-owned kind still levels it up (field pickup = temporary level, permanent reward = permanent level).
- **Determinism:** selection must stay injectable-rng deterministic; no wall-clock or `Math.random()` reads inside the new pure helpers.
- **No catalogue removals and no weight retuning:** the cap gates which ids may be drawn, not relative weights. `GameRules.powerUpWeights` / `weaponWeights` keep their meaning for the ids that remain eligible.
- **No individual rebalancing:** the six-slot cap is the balance change; per-item power tuning is out of scope.

## Existing state

- **"Power-up database":** `src/powerups/types.ts` — `PowerUpEntry` / `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` (16 power-ups); `POWER_UP_WEIGHT_IDS` (power-ups) and `WEAPON_WEIGHT_IDS` (weapon drops) in `src/core/rules.ts`; `WEAPON_DROP_IDS`/`CHOICE_POOL` list weapon drops alongside.
- **Permanent ownership (power-ups):** `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — `PowerUpLevelStore.collect(id, permanent)`, `permanentGrants(id)`, `getLevels()` (permanent kinds only) and `getEffectiveLevel`/`getTempStacks` for temporary pickups.
- **Permanent ownership (weapons):** `src/entities/Player.ts` — `equipWeapon(id, permanent)`, `getPermanentWeaponLevel(id)`, `getWeaponLevels()` (permanent kinds only), `getTempWeaponStacks`; `resetWeaponLevels()` on run restart. The cannon can never be permanently granted (`isTimedWeapon` guard) and `reset` is not a `WeaponId`.
- **Game spawn path:** `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_maybeDropPowerUp()` rolls the level-resolved drop chance, then spawns `this.dropSpawner.next()`. The spawner is built once by `buildDefaultDropSpawner()` (`src/scenes/core/dropLayer.ts`) as a `WeightedRandomSpawner<DropId>` over `POWER_UP_WEIGHT_IDS + WEAPON_WEIGHT_IDS`, with weights from `src/core/rules.ts`. A small asteroid also rolls an additive deterministic `extra_life` drop.
- **Gym spawn paths:** `GymFormationScene._spawnPowerUpDrop()` (`powerUpSpawner`), `GymPowerUpsUtility`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymPowerUpLeveling`, `GymWeapons`, `GymLevel` — deterministic round-robin spawners.
- **Hold-full choice:** `src/powerups/choice.ts` — `CHOICE_POOL`, `buildChoiceCandidates()`, `drawWeightedWithoutReplacement()`, `OWNED_UPGRADE_BONUS_WEIGHT`; `chooseOptions()` is consumed by `PlayScene` and every gym, and the mini-boss reward reuses `buildOwnedLevelUpOptions()` (`src/powerups/unlocks.ts`).
- **Effects application:** `EffectsRegistry.applyCollect()` routes a collection to the power-up store's temporary stack or permanent grant; `Player.equipWeapon(…, permanent)` records weapon grants. No cap on distinct kinds exists today.
- **Docs of record:** `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 (catalogue/table) and §4.5 (hold-full choice), `docs/BALANCING.md` (drop/choice balance), `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1 (parity convention), `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md`.

## Desired change

- Add `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP = 6` and an `availableWhenSlotsFull` flag on `PowerUpEntry` (Extra Life `true`, Mystery UFO `true`).
- Add a pure shared helper module (e.g. `src/powerups/slots.ts`) that, given the permanently-owned power-up ids, the permanently-owned weapon drop ids and the catalogues, answers: slots used, slots free, and whether a drop id may be drawn/offered. It owns the shared-pool and exemption rules — no `id === '…'` branches anywhere else.
- Apply that helper at the two decision points, both shared with the gyms:
  1. **drop selection** — the weighted draw excludes non-owned, non-exempt ids once the pool is full, for power-ups and weapons alike;
  2. **choice candidate construction** — `buildChoiceCandidates` excludes base entries that would create a seventh permanent kind once the pool is full, while owned level-up offers, exempt entries and the remaining candidates survive.
- Keep the below-cap path byte-for-byte equivalent in distribution (eligible set unchanged, weights unchanged).
- Cover with unit tests (helper + spawner + choice), integration tests (`PlayScene`), gym parity coverage, and documentation updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/types.ts` — add `availableWhenSlotsFull?: boolean` to `PowerUpEntry`; set `true` on `extra_life` and `mystery_ufo`; document default `false`.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP = 6` (mirroring existing `POWER_UP_*` constants).
- `src/powerups/slots.ts` *(new)* + `src/powerups/slots.test.ts` — pure shared-pool accounting and eligibility (power-ups + weapon drops, exemptions included).
- `src/powerups/spawner.ts` — let a draw consult an eligibility predicate (or accept an eligible-id set) without weakening the all-zero-weight fallback.
- `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.ts` — a shared `drawNextDrop(spawner, slotState)` seam (built on `buildDefaultDropSpawner`) so every scene draws through one filtered path.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — pass the run's permanently-owned power-up and weapon ids into the drop draw (keep the asteroid `extra_life` path untouched).
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — gate brand-new non-exempt kinds out of `buildChoiceCandidates` at the cap (owned level-ups and exempt entries remain).
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` / `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` / `src/entities/Player.ts` — expose the owned-permanent-kind view consumed by the two gates (no new counter).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` — consume the same filtered draw path (no divergent copy).
- Tests: `src/powerups/slots.test.ts` (new), `src/powerups/spawner.test.ts`, `src/powerups/choice.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` (parity guard).
- Docs: `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.4 catalogue table + §4.5 choice), `docs/BALANCING.md`, `README.md` if it states power-up/weapon rules.

## Related work

- AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P — *As the levels progress increase the number of enemies and decrease the number of power ups* (level-resolved drop chance; the supply-side counterpart of this demand-side cap).
- AH-0MVLJEE7O008RX9X — *Add level-scaling module and tunable rules* (where `powerUpDropChanceAtLevel1/Max` live; candidate home for a tunable cap).
- AH-0MV8GPGBL009M0D8 — *Smart Bomb is too powerful* (precedent for a single-item dominance fix; this item fixes dominance by accumulation instead).
- AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6 / AH-0MUV5CLVQ006V9HR — power-up level curves and the `GymPowerUpLeveling` parity gym (the permanent-grant model this cap counts).
- AH-0MUTPEIZ5002FIJP — *P10 power-up identity — catalogue, spawn pool, choice pool and icon* (established that spawn pool and choice pool are catalogue-derived; the cap must not break that invariant).
- AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1 — gym↔game parity convention + duplicate-body guard.
- AH-0MVL9P2SF009QFON — shared level-up option builder used by hold-full choice and mini-boss reward (the choice gate must be applied at the shared builder seam, not duplicated).
- AH-0MUCST4M7008O9CX — *Pluggable power-up choice strategy and permanent-effect support* (the `ChoiceStrategy` seam the choice gate extends).
- AH-0MUQOVYZU0073OUV — *Feature: Permanent mineral-choice weapon leveling* (permanent weapon-grant semantics; weapons now share this item's slot pool).

## Risks and assumptions

- **All-zero-weight fallback:** `WeightedRandomSpawner` falls back to the first entry when every weight is zero, so exclusion must not be implemented by zeroing weights — it must be an eligibility filter applied before/while sampling.
- **Empty eligible set:** if all six owned kinds are currently unofferable and no exemption applies, the eligible set must never be empty; the draw must degrade to exempt/weapon entries rather than crash or always return one id.
- **Shared-pool starvation (design consequence):** because weapons share the six slots, a weapon-heavy build can consume the pool before any power-up reward is taken. This is the producer's chosen semantics (Q1 answer (c)); the docs must state it so it is not later mistaken for a bug. Balance evidence may need re-recording (out of scope).
- **Weapons granted by other permanent paths:** mini-boss unlocks/upgrades that set a permanent weapon level ≥ 1 also occupy a slot (derived from the same store); a document + test should pin that behaviour so the pool cannot be over-filled silently.
- **Test churn:** `src/core/rules.test.ts` and `src/powerups/choice.test.ts` assert the catalogue-complete pool; those assertions need an explicit "below cap" context.
- **Bot/balance evaluation drift:** `src/ai/eval/*` simulates campaigns and will see a different late-game loadout; re-recording bot evidence is *not* in scope unless a gate fails (record as a linked follow-up if needed).
- **Scope-creep risk:** HUD slot readout (`N/6`), persisting slots in checkpoints/saved runs, capping the mini-boss weapon unlock pool separately, and rebalancing individual power-up/weapon strength are out of scope; each becomes a linked work item rather than extra scope here.
- **Assumption (A1, resolved by Q1 answer (c)):** one shared pool of six across power-up and weapon kinds; field pickups excluded.
- **Assumption (A3):** no new player-facing HUD/UX surface is required by this item (producer did not request one; if wanted, it becomes an explicit AC or a linked item).
- **Assumption (A4):** the cap is a named code constant (default 6), not a persisted `GameRules` setting.
- **Assumption (A5):** the cap applies in the gyms as well as the game (parity); no gym is exempted.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 — What consumes a slot?** *Answer (producer):* **"c, field pickups are excluded"** — one shared pool of six across power-up *and* weapon kinds; temporary field-pickup stacks never consume a slot. **Resolved:** slots = distinct permanently-owned drop kinds (power-up permanent grants + weapon permanent levels), derived from the existing stores; no new counter. Source: interactive producer reply on AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF.
- **Q2 — Does the hold-full choice also stop offering new kinds at the cap?** *Answer (producer):* **"a"** — yes, the choice is gated too: at six filled slots it offers level-ups of owned items and available-when-full entries only, never a new non-exempt kind (mini-boss reward inherits the same gate through the shared option builder). **Resolved.** Source: interactive producer reply.
- **Q3 — Exemption flag and drops already on screen?** *Answer (producer):* **"a (Mystery UFO can also have the flag true)"** — the flag is `availableWhenSlotsFull` on the power-up catalogue entry (default `false`), set for **Extra Life and Mystery UFO**; drops of non-owned kinds already on screen when the sixth slot fills remain collectible for their temporary effect and simply stop spawning. **Resolved.** Source: interactive producer reply.
- **Assumption A3 (recorded, not contradicted):** no new HUD slot readout is required — if the producer wants an `N/6` indicator it becomes an explicit AC or a linked follow-up item.
- **Assumption A4 (recorded, not contradicted):** the cap ships as a named constant rather than a persisted `GameRules` field.
- **Assumption A5 (recorded, not contradicted):** gyms obey the same cap (parity).
- **Q4–Q7 (answered 2026-10-27 by producer, see blocking comment AH-C0MVRC08UJ009D0CM):** Q4(a) temporary pickups occupy a slot while held and free it on expiry, and a hold-full at full slots offers only items currently in the slots; Q5(b) block collection of a non-owned non-exempt drop at the cap with a distinct not-collectable SFX; Q6(a) the choice gate follows the union; Q7(a) exempt entries never occupy a slot.
- **Research note:** duplicate-work check performed (`wl search` on "powerup slots limit", "powerup cap", "power-up limit", "spawn pool", "hold-full choice pool", "too powerful", "power creep") — no item (open or completed) implements a permanent loadout cap, so this item is not a duplicate. Closest completed work is the level-scaled power-up *supply* reduction (AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P) and the Smart Bomb power reduction (AH-0MV8GPGBL009M0D8); both are related, neither covers loadout breadth.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUQOVYZU0073OUV** – Feature: Permanent mineral-choice weapon leveling (completed)
- **AH-0MTV7RITM009LJF6** – Make weapons both cumalative and time out (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: 0muu2qje2007jnr6, 0muv5clvq006v9hr, 0mv8gpgbl009m0d8, 0mvht1m6o003pu7p, 0mvl9p2sf009qfon (+507 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0muu2qje2007jnr6, 0muv5clvq006v9hr, 0mv8gpgbl009m0d8, 0mvht1m6o003pu7p, 0mvl9p2sf009qfon (+504 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mugzdtfx004rbd1, 0mvht1m6o003pu7p, accept, accounting, add (+433 more)

## Plan: decomposition (plan skill, 2026-10-25)

Effort/risk pre-check returned `decision: plan` (effort Small, risk Medium); the plan-approval gate returned `request_approval: false` (approval is requested only for Extra Large effort **and** High/Severe risk), so no approval pause was needed. The brief's own Appendix already carried producer answers Q1–Q3, so no new questions were required.

**Phasing (vertical slices, test-first).** Every phase is a test + implementation pair so each slice is reviewable end-to-end; the docs phase closes the item. Between phases the next item's description is re-read and updated against what actually shipped.

| # | Work item | Type | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Test the six-slot accounting and exemption flag (AH-0MVNT2SD300874CP) | task | — |
| 2 | Shared six-slot helper, cap constant and exemption flag (AH-0MVNT2TEK001BNQ4) | feature | 1 |
| 3 | Test drop gating at full slots and below-cap parity (AH-0MVNT2XHB000YR2Z) | task | 2 |
| 4 | Gate the shared drop draw on the six-slot pool (AH-0MVNT2YGD003N8NR) | feature | 3 |
| 5 | Test hold-full choice gating at full slots (AH-0MVNT2Z89005OPKJ) | task | 2 |
| 6 | Gate choice candidates at full slots (AH-0MVNT2ZXK009Z5VU) | feature | 5 |
| 7 | Prove gym↔game parity and run-scoped slot state (AH-0MVNT30OT0074NNM) | task | 4, 6 |
| 8 | Document the six-slot cap and exemption flag (AH-0MVNT31C50065EE0) | docs | 4, 6 |

**Items 3–4 and 5–6 are independent branches** (drop draw vs choice pool) after item 2, so they may be implemented in either order; item 7 and item 8 need both.

**Acceptance-criteria coverage** (manual traceability check — the parent ACs are a numbered list, which the automated `tree_coverage` extractor does not parse, so coverage was verified directly; Jaccard scores of the best-matching child AC: AC1 0.84 (item 1), AC2 0.97 (item 4), AC3 0.97 (item 3), AC4 0.98 (items 5/6), AC5 0.65 (item 1), AC6 0.98 (item 7), AC7 0.96 (item 8)):

- AC1 (cap and shared accounting) → items 1, 2
- AC2 (spawn gating at full slots) → items 3, 4, 7
- AC3 (no behaviour change below the cap) → items 3, 4
- AC4 (choice gating at full slots) → items 5, 6
- AC5 (data-driven exemption flag) → items 1, 2
- AC6 (parity and run scope) → items 4, 7
- AC7 (documentation and suite) → item 8

No catalogue removal, no weight retuning and no per-item rebalancing are planned — the cap gates eligibility only, as the constraints require.

## Change of plan — 2026-10-25 producer audit (authoritative, supersedes parts of AC1–AC7)

The producer rejected the shipped implementation with this audit verdict (recorded
in the audit store, author `rgardler`, audited 2026-10-25T22:54:56Z):

> Rejected by manual review. Change of plan the slots should be limited to 6 slots
> for both permanent and temporary (field) pickups.

That verdict supersedes the earlier Q1 answer (c) ("field pickups excluded") and
the AC text that says field pickups never consume a slot. It is also **not** what
shipped in v0.1.15: `src/powerups/slots.ts` derives occupancy from the permanent
grants only, and the GDD §4.4 / `docs/BALANCING.md` say so explicitly. The delta
therefore has to be re-planned as a new increment on top of the eight closed
children (which stay closed).

### What the change touches

- `src/powerups/slots.ts` — occupancy (`resolveSlotState`), eligibility
  (`isWithinSlotPool` / `eligibleDropIds`) and the "full" definition.
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — the candidate gate at full slots.
- `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.ts` / `CombatCoreScene.ts` / `PlayScene.ts` + the gym
  scenes — the callers that resolve the slot state.
- Tests that pin the current semantics (`src/powerups/slots.test.ts`,
  `src/powerups/slots.weaponLevels.test.ts`, `src/powerups/__tests__/choice.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.test.ts`, `src/powerups/slots.parity.test.ts`) and the
  docs assertions (`src/powerUpSlotsDocs.test.ts`).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4/§4.5 and `docs/BALANCING.md`.

Temporary state is already exposed per kind (`PowerUpLevelStore.getTempStacks(id)` /
`getEffectiveLevel(id)`, `Player.getTempWeaponStacks(id)` / `getWeaponLevel(id)`), so
a temporary-aware occupancy can still be **derived** (no new counter) for option (a)
of Q4 below.

### Resolved — producer answers 2026-10-27 (all four answered; recorded in the
blocking comment AH-C0MVRC08UJ009D0CM)

- **Q4 → (a)** — a kind occupies a slot while held permanently **or** temporarily;
  the slot frees when the field-pickup window expires. Occupancy stays derived from
  the existing stores. With the answer came an explicit note: **if a hold-full is
  offered while all slots are full then only offer items that are currently in the
  slots** — this is AC4's gate.
- **Q5 → (b)** — a non-owned, non-exempt drop is blocked at the cap (a collection
  gate), and **there must be an SFX indicating it is not collectable** — this is
  AC8.
- **Q6 → (a)** — the choice gate follows the union: at full slots only items
  currently in the slots are offered (level-ups of permanent owned kinds, base
  picks for temp-held kinds, exempt entries).
- **Q7 → (a)** — exempt entries (`extra_life`, `mystery_ufo`) never occupy a slot;
  the flag exempts them from the count as well as from the spawn gate.

### Assumptions that stand unless contradicted

- A3 no HUD `N/6` readout; A4 the cap stays the named constant `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP = 6`;
  A5 the gyms obey the same rule; the permanent cannon and the `reset` utility never
  count; a repeat pickup of an already-slotted kind levels that slot and never adds a
  second one.
- Existing docs/tests asserting "field pickups never consume a slot" are **rewritten**,
  not deleted, once the decisions land.


## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-25 — plan skill: created 8 child items (4 test-first items before their implementation pairs, plus parity evidence and docs), wired 9 dependency edges, verified AC coverage, advanced stage to `plan_complete`. No existing content removed; producer answers Q1–Q3 and assumptions A3–A5 carried forward unchanged.

## Goal (tracer-bullet vertical slice)

Ship the first end-to-end music slice: the menu/attract ambient track ("Star Drift", Lydian) played through the existing shared AudioContext, driven by a minimal music state machine, with the autoplay/gesture guard and an independent music volume control.

This slice cuts through every layer — baked asset, playback facade, state machine, scene wiring, settings, tests, docs — so later slices extend a proven path rather than a horizontal layer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The menu/attract state plays the baked "Star Drift" Lydian ambient stem as a seamless loop.
- [ ] Music starts only after a user gesture, honouring the AudioContext resume discipline (GDD 7.3), and reuses the single shared AudioContext owned by the playback provider.

# Bot tuning scene is not using the same gameplay objects as the main game

## Problem statement

Gym scenes are the canonical parity reference for the shipped game, yet the
level-launch gym path (`GymLevel`, which `GymBotTuning` extends) carries its own
inline wave-spawn implementation that has drifted from `PlayScene`. A designer
tuning the bot therefore watches enemies that do **not** behave as they do in
play, which invalidates the tuning signal the gym exists to provide.

## Findings from repo investigation (intake, 2026-10-27)

The reported symptom is real and is one of several divergences in the same spawn
seam:

1. **Phasers spawn in a line then snap to their ring (reported bug).**
   `PlayScene._spawnEnemy` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:1647`) and
   `GymFormationScene` (`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts:1755`) both
   resolve an orbital entity's wormhole-transit destination through the entity's
   live `formationSlot()` seam (AH-0MVEXVME1004SIIS). `GymLevel.spawnWave`
   (`src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts:299`) does not: its resolver returns the grid
   slot (`startX + driftX + col * spacingX`), so Phasers transit to a straight
   line and then snap onto the orbit when the spawn window ends. Because
   `GymBotTuning extends GymLevel` (`src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts:149`), the
   bot-tuning gym reproduces exactly the symptom the producer reported.
   Regression coverage exists for `PlayScene`
   (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:6697`) and `GymFodderEnemies`
   (`src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.test.ts:396`) but **not** for
   `GymLevel`/`GymBotTuning`.

2. **Launched-level enemies never fire.** `PlayScene._spawnEnemy` assigns
   `entity.shootEnabled = spawn.shootEnabled`; `GymLevel.spawnWave` never
   assigns it, and `BaseEnemy._shootEnabled` defaults to `false`
   (`src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts:97`), so every `tryFire*` method returns nothing.
   Campaign levels 4+ carry `shootEnabled: true`
   (`src/waves/Formations.ts:157`), so a level launched from the curve editor or
   played in the bot-tuning gym is silently non-threatening. `GymLevel`'s own
   tests work around this by setting `victim.shootEnabled = true` by hand
   (`src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.test.ts:599`), which is itself evidence of the gap.

3. **March formations do not march.** `PlayScene` keeps a rigid `marchState`
   block and re-anchors march spawns (`_resetMarchFormation`,
   `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:1737`); `GymLevel` has only horizontal `driftX`.
   Campaign levels 2–10 contain `march` groups
   (`src/waves/Formations.ts:381-424`), so the launched block renders as a
   static line instead of the stepping/dropping block the game shows.

4. **The transit resolver is copied three times.** Each spawn site inlines the
   same non-trivial logic ("autonomous-mover exemption → orbital-slot branch →
   live slot / offset fallback"). The repo-wide duplicate-body guard
   (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`, `EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS`)
   does not cover this seam, which is why the third copy could drift unnoticed.
   `GymLevel` also keeps a legacy in-place spawn path used when no wormhole
   origin is supplied — dead for gameplay but still a second code path to keep
   honest.

5. **Divergences that must be preserved (already documented).** `GymPlayer`'s
   obstacle course, `GymWeapons`' AOE training targets, the flat supply cadence
   in `GymFormationScene`-derived gyms, gym-only HUD/tuning panels and the
   absence of run telemetry are intentional and recorded in
   `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1 and `docs/BALANCING.md`. The
   fix must not "unify" these away.

## Users and example user stories

- **Bot-tuning designer (primary):** "As a designer tuning the bot in
  `GymBotTuning`, I want the enemies I watch to spawn, transit, march and fire
  exactly as they do in the shipped game, so the tuning I save transfers to the
  attract demo and recordings."
- **Gameplay developer:** "As a developer landing a spawn/formation fix in
  `PlayScene`, I want the gyms to consume the same seam, so I cannot leave a gym
  behind without the test suite failing."
- **Level/curve designer:** "As a designer launching a campaign level from the
  curve editor, I want the launched level to be a faithful preview of the
  shipped level."

## Existing state

- Three spawn implementations: `PlayScene._spawnEnemy` (game),
  `GymFormationScene` (formation gyms), `GymLevel.spawnWave` (level/bot-tuning
  gyms). Only the first two honour the `formationSlot` seam.
- Spawn presentation (`startSpawnAnimation`, wormhole open/close, spawn
  protection) is already shared via `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts`; what diverges is
  the **destination resolver**, the per-enemy `shootEnabled` hand-off and the
  march block.
- Gym↔game parity coverage is extensive for combat, drops, movement, boss
  motion and projectile lifecycle, but has no coverage for the start-of-wave
  spawn presentation on the level-launch path.
- The capture/scripted-scene seam (`src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.ts`) is already
  consumed by `GymFormationScene` and `GymLevel` only, and the scene registry
  (`scripts/capture-scenes.mjs`) already lists every `Gym<Name>` as capturable
  except the parameterised `GymFodderEnemies`/`GymLevel`.

## Desired change

1. Extract the wormhole-transit destination resolution into **one** shared
   helper under `src/scenes/core/` and make all four spawn sites
   (`PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel`, `GymBoss` minions) consume it,
   so the orbital-slot seam, the autonomous-mover exemption and the live-slot
   tracking can no longer drift.
2. Propagate the wave's per-enemy `shootEnabled` (and the formation RNG) through
   the `GymLevel` spawn path exactly as `PlayScene` does.
3. Bring the march block to the level-launch path (or consume the shared march
   state) so launched march waves step and drop as they do in the game.
4. Register the new seam in the duplicate-body guard and add cross-scene
   equivalence tests that boot `PlayScene` and `GymLevel`/`GymBotTuning` with the
   same seeded orbital/march wave and assert identical spawn trajectories and
   identical fire cadence.
5. Sweep **every** gym scene (`src/scenes/gym/`, including the generic
   `GymFormationScene` and the level/bot-tuning path) against `PlayScene` for
   enabled-object parity and record the result in a single parity matrix. **Fix
   every real divergence found in this item** (each with a test), rather than
   deferring them; documented, intentional divergences stay, with their reason
   recorded in the matrix.
6. Adopt the scripted-scene `setup` seam in **every** gym in this item: each gym
   applies the shared `applySceneSetup` applier and exposes whatever
   scene-specific scenario parameters it needs (enemy roster, formation, level,
   toggles) through the capture scene config, so any gym can be driven from
   `examples/scenes.json` and recorded. Extend the config validation and the
   `WATCHABLE_GYM_SCENE_KEYS` / parameterised-scene contracts accordingly.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — Booting `PlayScene` and `GymLevel` (and therefore `GymBotTuning`) with the same seeded orbital wave produces the same per-frame transit target for every Phaser: each frame's destination equals the entity's live `formationSlot()`, and no enemy is ever placed on a straight line then snapped to the ring. Verified by a cross-scene equivalence test that fails on the pre-change code (red-before / green-after).
- [ ] AC2 — A launched wave with `shootEnabled: true` fires in `GymLevel` / `GymBotTuning` at the same cadence and bullet speed as the same wave in `PlayScene` (shared dispatcher, real scene clock). Verified by a parity test, not a hand-set `shootEnabled` in the test.
- [ ] AC3 — A launched `march` wave steps/drops in the gym exactly as the game's block does for the same `dt` sequence. Verified by a parity test.
- [ ] AC4 — The spawn-transit destination logic is defined exactly **once** repo-wide, is registered in `EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS`, and every spawn site (`PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel`, `GymBoss`) resolves to it; the duplicate-body guard fails if a copy is re-introduced.
- [ ] AC5 — A gym↔game parity matrix document records, for **every** gym scene under `src/scenes/gym/` (including the generic `GymFormationScene` and the level/bot-tuning path), which shipped gameplay objects it runs, whether it inherits the shipped start-of-wave/combat code, and — where it diverges — the reason. Every real divergence identified by the sweep is **fixed in this item** with a regression test; retained divergences are only those already documented as intentional and each is re-justified in the matrix.
- [ ] AC6 — Every gym applies the shared scripted-scene `setup` seam and exposes its scenario parameters through the capture scene config, so any gym can be launched and recorded from `examples/scenes.json`; the scene-config validator rejects unsupported/parameterised targets with a clear error, and the `WATCHABLE_GYM_SCENE_KEYS` registry contract and its pinning test are updated.
- [ ] AC7 — `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1 (and `AGENTS.md` § Game Architecture Conventions where the rule text changes) explain the shared spawn seam and point at the parity matrix; the docs guard test still passes.
- [ ] AC8 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries (including the scripted-scene/gym capture documentation).
- [ ] AC9 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No balance changes. Behavioural differences introduced by this item must be a
  *fix toward* the game's behaviour, except where the producer explicitly asks
  for a new gym capability (scripted-scene setup, AC6).
- Must not "fix" documented intentional divergences (obstacle course, AOE
  practice targets, flat formation-gym supply cadence, gym HUD); each must keep
  its documented reason.
- Must not regress the automation that consumes the gyms: the capture CLI and
  `sceneSetup` appliers, Watch Demo / demo mode, the bot-tuning store, and the
  `WATCHABLE_GYM_SCENE_KEYS` registry contract.
- Scope is deliberately broad (producer direction: sweep and fix all in this
  item). If the sweep uncovers a divergence that cannot be fixed without a
  separate design decision, record it as a blocker with evidence on this item
  rather than silently expanding the design.
- The item is expected to be decomposed into child items at the plan stage
  (shared seam, spawn-parity fixes, gym sweep, scripted-scene adoption, docs);
  the ACs above are the whole-item contract.
- The reported symptom must be reproducible before the fix and demonstrably
  fixed after it (red-before / green-after per repo convention).
- Implementation runs in the item's own worktree per `AGENTS.md`.

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/spawnTransit.ts` — **new** shared destination-resolver seam
  (orbital slot / offset fallback / autonomous exemption / live-slot tracking).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — consume the shared seam from `_spawnEnemy`;
  keep march state as the single source for block anchoring.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — replace its inline resolver.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts` — consume the seam, propagate `shootEnabled` and
  the formation RNG, adopt the march block or document why not.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts` — inherits the fix; update its divergence
  note if the scenario description changes.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` — minion spawn keeps the in-place (no-transit)
  behaviour through the same seam.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — register the new helper
  in `EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS`; add cross-scene spawn equivalence coverage.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/levelParity.test.ts` — spawn/fire/march parity assertions.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (§5.1) and a new gym parity matrix
  document (e.g. `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`) listing every gym scene, the shipped
  objects it runs and its divergences.
- `src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts` — docs guard update if the rule text
  changes.
- `src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.ts` — extend the applier so every gym can take a
  setup; `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` and its tests — extend the config schema,
  parameterised-target handling and `WATCHABLE_GYM_SCENE_KEYS` contract.
- `src/scenes/gym/*.ts` (all 14 gym scenes, including `GymCurveSequencer`,
  `GymPlayer`, `GymWeapons`, `GymPowerUps*`, `GymWeaponLeveling`,
  `GymPowerUpLeveling`, `GymMinerals`, `GymCentipede`, `GymMiniBoss`) — apply the
  setup seam and fix any divergence the sweep finds.
- `examples/scenes.json` and `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — demonstrate a
  scripted scene for each gym family.

## Related work

- Wormhole/transit/formation-slot lineage: AH-0MV8BSMXC0097KLW (enemies emerge
  from the wormhole), AH-0MVDW3T9R0054HG6 (transit movement, parity, docs),
  AH-0MVDW3R7300979DC (scene-level transit tests), AH-0MVEXVME1004SIIS (Phasers
  spawn in a line then snap), AH-0MVF4P31M0033RAC (shared orbital geometry and
  orbital transit destination), AH-0MVF4OVY6000DZE8 (orbital geometry tests),
  AH-0MV8BR9Y70079TKC (wormhole placement), AH-0MV9KHLV8006GMX6 (wormhole
  lifecycle).
- Gym parity principle and guards: AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1 (docs the parity
  principle), AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P / AH-0MVLJF6ZD00164MG (level gym scaling
  parity), AH-0MV9AWR7A0084XJ0 (bot-tuning gym scenario parity gap — same class
  of defect, already completed).
- Scripted-scene / capture lineage: AH-0MVPJ3NSK008V5VB (scripted scenes for
  video, open, needs producer review), AH-0MVNW8VNN004FFK1 (shared scene-setup
  applier), AH-0MVNW90FB003H3KM (setup determinism seed), AH-0MVE01EY0008QEVX
  (generated-level scenes), AH-0MV6MFDYG001E6PL (Watch Demo flies saved
  bot-tuning).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 (blocking) — implementation shape.** "Should the fix land as one shared
  spawn-transit seam consumed by `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel`
  and `GymBoss`, or as a minimal local patch to `GymLevel.spawnWave`? Options:
  (a) extract a shared seam in `src/scenes/core/`, consume it at all four spawn
  sites, register it in the duplicate-body guard, and add cross-scene spawn
  equivalence tests; (b) minimal patch — add the `formationSlot` branch and the
  `shootEnabled` hand-off to `GymLevel.spawnWave` only, with tests, leaving the
  three copies in place; (c) other. **Recommended: (a)** — this is the third
  divergent copy of the same resolver and the guard did not catch it, so a local
  patch leaves the next drift unguarded." — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-27): "A"**
  ⇒ option (a): one shared spawn-transit seam in `src/scenes/core/`, consumed
  by all four spawn sites, registered in the duplicate-body guard, with
  cross-scene spawn equivalence tests. Source: interactive producer reply on the
  resume prompt.
- **Q2 (blocking) — audit depth and deliverable.** "How far should 'check all
  others too' go? Options: (a) sweep every gym scene against `PlayScene` for
  start-of-wave/spawn and enabled-object parity, publish a parity matrix, fix the
  real divergences found in this item and file child items for anything that
  should not be fixed now; (b) fix only the spawn-path divergences named in this
  brief (Phaser orbit, `shootEnabled`, march) with a test per gym, no matrix;
  (c) sweep and fix every divergence found, however large, before closing.
  **Recommended: (a)** — bounded, auditable, and it prevents an open-ended
  fix-everything scope while still honouring the request to check all gyms."
  — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-27): "A sweep and fix"** ⇒ interpreted as (a)'s
  sweep + parity matrix **plus** (c)'s fix-in-this-item, consistent with the Q3
  answer "fix all in this item": every gym is swept against `PlayScene`, the
  matrix is published, and every real divergence found is fixed here rather than
  deferred to child items. Recorded as a documented assumption; if the producer
  meant "sweep + defer some fixes" that is a plan-stage adjustment, not a change
  of intent. Source: interactive producer reply.
- **Q3 (blocking) — scripted-scene adoption.** "Should this item also configure
  every gym to run under the scripted-scene `setup` seam? Options: (a) track it
  separately — this item stays a parity fix and a follow-up child item extends
  `applySceneSetup` to every gym and makes gym scenarios expressible in
  `examples/scenes.json`; (b) include it here — extend the setup applier to all
  gyms (including roster/formation/toggle fields, since `GymFodderEnemies` and
  `GymLevel` are parameterised) and make every gym capturable from config;
  (c) document only — describe how gyms can be scripted, no code. **Recommended:
  (a)** — the parity fix is already large and the setup extension depends on it;
  keeping the capture work in its own item preserves reviewable, testable
  scope." — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-27): "fix all in this item"** ⇒ option
  (b): the scripted-scene `setup` adoption for every gym is in scope for this
  item (AC6), not deferred. Source: interactive producer reply.

# Test: tracked-CSV suite-write regression guard

**Parent:** AH-0MVKYQWSW0067F12 (plan phase; test-first item — created first)

## Summary

Add the automated regression guard that proves a full-suite run never modifies the
tracked config CSVs (`src/data/ship-config.csv`, `src/data/enemy-configs.csv`,
`src/data/difficulty-curves.csv`) in **either** the active worktree **or** the main
checkout. This is the acceptance test for the parent bug: it must fail loudly when a
later change reintroduces a leaked CSV write.

## User story

As a developer/agent running the suite, I want the suite itself to assert that no tracked
CSV changed during the run, so a leaked write fails the run immediately instead of tripping
the implement dirty-tree gate hours later.

## Scope

- A Vitest `globalSetup`/teardown pair (new small module, e.g.
  `src/test/trackedCsvGuard.globalSetup.ts` plus a testable helper) registered in
  `vitest.config.ts` for both `unit` and `integration` projects.
- Snapshot the content hash (sha256) of the three tracked CSVs in the active checkout at
  suite start; resolve the main checkout via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` (worktrees
  share the main `.git`, so `dirname` of the common dir is the main checkout) and snapshot
  its CSVs too when the path differs and the files exist.
- On teardown, compare; if any file changed, throw with the offending path(s), the
  checkout, and the pre/post git diff hint so the failure is actionable.
- A pure unit test for the comparison/reporting helper (changed / unchanged / missing /
  non-git checkout cases) so the guard logic itself is covered without needing a leak.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Parent AC 1 (AH-0MVKYQWSW0067F12) covered by this item:** **No tracked-file writes from suites** — Running the audit-accepted full suite (`npm --silent test`: `unit` + `integration` projects) from a worktree leaves every tracked `src/data/*.csv` (`ship-config.csv`, `enemy-configs.csv`, `difficulty-curves.csv`) unchanged in **both** the active worktree and the main checkout. Verified by an automated pre/post `git status --porcelain` of both checkouts that runs as part of the change's tests (a regression guard the suite itself asserts).

- `npm --silent test` registers the guard for both projects; a full suite run leaves all
  three tracked CSVs byte-identical in the active checkout and the main checkout.
- The guard is proven effective: a deliberate in-test write to a tracked CSV (or a
  temporary mutation performed inside the guard's own unit test) makes the guard report the
  changed file and fail — the check is not vacuous.
- Guard degrades safely: outside a git repository, or when the main checkout path is
  unresolvable, it logs a skip reason and does not fail the run.
- Guard teardown never writes to the watched files and never itself dirties the tree
  (`git status --porcelain` is unchanged by a suite run apart from intended test output).
- The helper's unit tests pass and are included in the existing `unit` project selection.

## Key Files

- `src/test/trackedCsvGuard.ts` — hash/compare/report helper (pure, unit-testable).
- `src/test/trackedCsvGuard.test.ts` — unit tests for the helper.
- `src/test/trackedCsvGuard.globalSetup.ts` — Vitest global setup returning the teardown.
- `vitest.config.ts` — register `globalSetup` for the `unit` and `integration` projects.
- `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts` — reference for the tracked CSV list; do not duplicate logic.

## Minimal implementation (smallest end-to-end slice)

1. Helper: `snapshotTrackedCsvs(repoRoots: string[]) -> Map<path, hash>`,
   `diffSnapshots(before, after) -> string[]` and a formatter for the failure message.
2. Global setup: resolve the active root from `process.cwd()` and the main checkout from
   `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`; return a teardown closure that diffs and throws.
3. Unit-test the helper's diff/format paths, including a real temp-dir mutation.
4. Register in `vitest.config.ts` for both projects; run the changed-scope suite via
   `/skill:test` to confirm green.

## Notes / risks

- Do **not** shell out to `git status` for the assertion (porcelain output is noisier than
  content hashes and cannot distinguish checkouts); use content hashes and keep git only
  for locating the main checkout.
- The guard is expected to be committed **before** the fixes (TDD); it should pass on a
  clean run and only fail if a leak recurs.
- Overlap: `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts` already validates CSV *content* in the active
  checkout; this item adds the cross-checkout write guard, it does not replace the seed
  tests.

# Feature: CSV plugin root isolation and escape refusal

**Parent:** AH-0MVKYQWSW0067F12

## Summary

Replace the CSV dev-server plugin's implicit `process.cwd()` write root with an explicit,
verified root derived from the Vite-resolved project root, and refuse any request whose
resolved target escapes that root (no file I/O, HTTP error plus a logged reason).

## User story

As a test-suite/CI operator, I want the CSV plugin to be incapable of writing outside the
checkout it is serving, so a suite run can never clobber the main checkout's tracked CSVs
through a symlinked `node_modules` / mis-inferred project root.

## Scope

- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts`:
  - Resolve the root inside `configureServer` as
    `options.root ?? server.config.root` (Vite resolves `server.config.root` from the
    config file's directory, so it stays in the active checkout instead of following
    `process.cwd()`); keep `options.root` as an explicit override for the existing
    temp-fixture tests.
  - Add a containment guard: for both GET and PUT, `resolve(root, relPath)` must stay inside
    the resolved root (`path.relative` check plus a `..`/absolute-path check, not naive
    `startsWith`); otherwise respond `403` with
    `{ ok: false, error: 'target escapes project root' }` and log the reason, performing no
    filesystem access.
  - Update the `ConfigCsvPluginOptions.root` doc comment and the factory doc comment to
    describe the new root semantics.
- `vite.config.ts`: only touch if the plugin cannot self-derive the root; keep
  `configCsvPlugin()` optionless when `server.config.root` suffices.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Parent AC 2 (AH-0MVKYQWSW0067F12) covered by this item:** **Root isolation in the plugin** — The CSV plugin never resolves write targets to a checkout other than the active project root: the implicit `process.cwd()` default is replaced by an explicit, verified root (derived from the Vite-resolved root, or an explicit option), and any request whose resolved target escapes the active root is refused with no file I/O (HTTP error + logged reason). Existing explicit-root test fixtures keep working unchanged.

- With no `root` option, a plugin configured against a fake `ViteDevServer` whose
  `config.root` is a temp dir writes only inside that temp dir — never to
  `process.cwd()` (asserted by a test that sets `process.cwd()` elsewhere and checks the
  cwd CSV is untouched).
- A request whose `relPath` escapes the root (`../` traversal, URL-encoded traversal,
  absolute path) is refused with HTTP 403, no file created/modified on disk, and a
  logged reason; covered for both GET and PUT.
- Existing explicit-root fixtures in `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.test.ts` and
  `src/core/configStore.integration.test.ts` keep passing unchanged.
- Valid in-root writes keep atomic-write (temp file + rename) behaviour and the existing
  upsert/append semantics; `isDevServer`/`apply: 'serve'` gating is unchanged.
- The plugin's own tests pass in the `unit` project selection.

## Key Files

- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` — root resolution, containment guard, doc comments.
- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.test.ts` — new default-root and escape-refusal tests.
- `vite.config.ts` — only if an explicit root must be passed; otherwise untouched.
- `src/core/configStore.integration.test.ts` — regression check only (explicit root path).
- `src/core/csv.ts` — reference for the codec/validation helpers; not expected to change.

## Minimal implementation (smallest end-to-end slice)

1. Move `root` resolution into `configureServer`; keep `options.root` precedence.
2. Add `isWithinRoot(root, filePath)` helper plus a `403` refusal branch used by both
   handlers before any `existsSync`/`readFileSync`/`atomicWrite`.
3. Add the two tests (default-root isolation, escape refusal for GET and PUT).
4. Update the option/factory doc comments; run the changed-scope suite via `/skill:test`.

## Notes / risks

- Do not weaken the guard for the legit dev workflow: `npm run dev` in the active checkout
  must still persist saves to the committed CSVs (AH-0MTZWZ9TE009CVUA).
- Symlink caveat: compare real paths (`realpath`) where available so a symlinked
  `node_modules` cannot make a legitimate active root look foreign — but a *target* outside
  the root must always be refused.
- Guard reads as well as writes (the parent AC says "any request"); this is deliberate and
  should be noted in the code comment.

# Feature: Test-mode write guard in configStore

**Parent:** AH-0MVKYQWSW0067F12

## Summary

Add a test-harness guard in `src/core/configStore.ts` so `saveShipConfig`,
`saveEnemyConfig` and `saveDifficultyCurves` can never write a tracked repository file
under vitest: in test mode they update the in-memory registry only and perform no network
I/O.

## User story

As a test author, I want store saves under vitest to be hermetic (registry-only, no disk,
no network), so a test can exercise save behaviour without any chance of PUTing through a
live dev server into a checkout.

## Scope

- `src/core/configStore.ts`:
  - Add `isTestMode()` = `import.meta.env.MODE === 'test'`, next to `isDev()`/`isSsr()`,
    with a doc comment explaining why it exists (belt-and-braces against the relative
    `/api/csv/...` fetch resolving against the happy-dom origin).
  - In each save function, after the `isDev()` gate, short-circuit in test mode: apply the
    same registry mutation the success path applies (including the difficulty-curve
    `generation` normalisation), skip `putCsv`, skip `reReadRegistry`, return `{ ok: true }`.
  - Document the resulting save semantics (registry-only in test mode) on the three
    exported save functions.
- `src/core/configStore.test.ts`: direct unit tests for the guard.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Parent AC 3 (AH-0MVKYQWSW0067F12) covered by this item:** **Test-mode write guard in the store** — Under the vitest/test harness (`import.meta.env.MODE === 'test'` detected in `configStore.ts`), `saveShipConfig`/`saveEnemyConfig`/`saveDifficultyCurves` must never write a tracked repository file: they either update the registry only (documented no-op wrt disk, preserving registry semantics used by tests) or route writes to an isolated temp fixture. A direct unit test covers each save function under test mode asserting no file on disk changes.

- Under `MODE === 'test'` (`vi.stubEnv('MODE', 'test')` with `DEV` true), each of
  `saveShipConfig`, `saveEnemyConfig` and `saveDifficultyCurves` resolves `{ ok: true }`
  while performing **no** `fetch` (asserted with a spy/stub that fails the test if called)
  and leaving every tracked CSV byte-identical (hash check).
- Registry semantics are preserved: after a test-mode ship save, `loadShipConfig()` (and the
  equivalent enemy/difficulty accessors) return the saved values; the difficulty-curve
  `generation` normalisation still applies.
- In non-test dev mode (`MODE` not `test`, `DEV` true) the existing write path is
  unchanged: the save still PUTs through `putCsv` and re-reads the registry (asserted with
  the existing fetch-bridge pattern in a temp root).
- Outside dev mode the existing `WRITE_UNAVAILABLE` behaviour is unchanged.
- All new and existing `src/core/configStore*.test.ts` tests pass in their projects.

## Key Files

- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `isTestMode()`, save-function short-circuit, doc comments.
- `src/core/configStore.test.ts` — test-mode guard unit tests.
- `src/core/configStore.integration.test.ts` — reference for the explicit-root fetch bridge
  pattern; adjust only if the guard changes its expectations.
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts` — reference for default ship/enemy values.

## Minimal implementation (smallest end-to-end slice)

1. Add `isTestMode()` beside `isDev()`/`isSsr()` with the rationale comment.
2. Add the guard branch to `saveShipConfig` (registry update + `{ ok: true }`), then mirror
   it for `saveEnemyConfig` and `saveDifficultyCurves`.
3. Unit-test each save function in test mode: no fetch, no disk change, registry updated.
4. One dev-mode control test proving the real write path still runs; run the changed-scope
   suite via `/skill:test`.

## Notes / risks

- Do not gate on `isDev() === false` (that would flip existing dev-mode assertions); the
  guard is an additional, earlier exit for `MODE === 'test'` only.
- A test-mode caller that expects a *failure* result (`ok: false`) must now stub the store
  function or assert the registry-only contract — check `GymPlayer.test.ts`,
  `GymFodderEnemies.test.ts` and gym save tests for such assumptions.
- Documented divergence: in test mode the registry is authoritative and disk is not, which
  matches how the mocked-store gym tests already behave.

## Summary

Close the escape route at the harness level: in the `integration` (happy-dom) project, a

  - for `/api/csv/...` requests without an installed bridge, rejects (or returns a
    synthetic `503` with a clear message) naming the test file and pointing at the bridge
    helper, without performing any network I/O.

  `src/core/configStore.integration.test.ts`.

  bridge; note the `configStore` test-mode guard as the second line of defence.

- **Parent AC 4 (AH-0MVKYQWSW0067F12) covered by this item:** **Escape route closed** — No test can PUT through a live dev-server endpoint by accident: relative `/api/csv/...` fetches in the happy-dom project must resolve against a test-controlled origin (explicit bridge/stub), never a stray `localhost` server that could answer from the main checkout. # Fail fast on unwritable --out and invalid tune CSV

## Goal (user story)
As a developer running tune-loop verification I want `--tune` to validate `--out` (and the
balance CSV path) before anything expensive starts, so an invalid path fails in seconds with
an actionable message instead of running both sweeps first and then hanging or dying.

## Problem
`scripts/evaluate.mjs` only touches the output directory after both batches have run:
`executeTune()` calls `mkdirSync(options.outputDir, {recursive: true})` *after* the candidate
sweep (line ~394) and `main()` does the same for the non-tune path (line ~441). The 2026-10-21
negative probe (`--out /proc/nope/x`, 2 games x 200 ticks) therefore ran both sweeps and then
stalled for 166.6 minutes before an external SIGKILL (parent item AH-0MVIKLOOJ0058Z9B).

## Expected behaviour
- `node scripts/evaluate.mjs --tune --set enemy-configs.csv boss.health=7 --games 2 --ticks 200 --out <unwritable>`
  exits non-zero in well under two seconds, printing a single clear diagnostic on stderr.
- The probe runs **before** `loadCore()` (no Vite SSR boot) and before any `--tune` sweep.
- The `--tune` CSV target (`src/data/<tuneFile>`) is validated up-front too: a missing or
  unreadable CSV fails fast with its own message instead of failing after a baseline sweep.

## Implementation sketch (smallest end-to-end slice)
1. Add an exported, unit-testable probe to `scripts/evaluate.mjs`, e.g.
   `ensureWritableOutputDir(dir)` → `{ok: true}` | `{ok: false, code, message}`:
   `mkdirSync(dir, {recursive: true})`, then write + `fsync` + unlink a sentinel file
   (`.evaluate-write-probe-<pid>`) so an unwritable-but-existing directory (`EACCES`) is
   caught, not just a non-creatable one (`ENOTDIR`, `EROFS`).
2. Export a matching `assertTuneInputs(csvPath)` (`readFileSync` probe) for the `--tune` CSV.
3. In `main()`, call the probes immediately after `parseEvaluateArgs`/`--help` handling and
   **before** `loadCore()`; on failure write `output directory not writable: <dir> (<code>)`
   (and the CSV equivalent) to stderr and return a non-zero exit code (2 — same class as the
   existing usage-error exit, documented in `EVALUATE_USAGE`).
4. Keep the late `mkdirSync` calls as a cheap idempotent safety net; do not duplicate the
   validity logic.
5. Update `EVALUATE_USAGE` and `docs/BALANCING.md` (§Tuning loop → "Guards and guarantees")
   with the fail-fast validation, and extend the doc guard
   (`src/ai/eval/balancingDocs.test.ts`) to assert the new statements.

## Key Files
- scripts/evaluate.mjs
- scripts/evaluate-failfast.test.ts
- scripts/evaluate-args.test.ts
- docs/BALANCING.md
- src/ai/eval/balancingDocs.test.ts

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The repro command fails fast (< 2 s) with a clear "output directory not writable" diagnostic and a non-zero exit, demonstrated after the fix (timings quoted in a work-item comment).
2. The writeability probe and CSV-path validation run before loadCore() and before any baseline or candidate sweep, proven by a test that observes no SSR boot on the failure path.
3. An unwritable-but-existing directory (EACCES) and a non-directory path (ENOTDIR) both fail fast, and the --tune CSV path is validated before the baseline sweep.
4. --tune with a valid --out still runs baseline -> edit -> re-run -> compare -> restore and exits 0; existing behaviour is preserved and existing evaluate/tune tests stay green.
5. CLI help (EVALUATE_USAGE) and docs/BALANCING.md mention the new validation, and the docs-guard test asserts it.
6. Unit tests cover the writeability probe and the CLI exit codes for each failure path, run under the project test policy (test skill).

# Journal the tune CSV edit so a hard kill cannot leave it dirty

## Goal (user story)
As a developer I want the tune/edit cycle crash-safe, so that even an external SIGKILL, OOM or
timeout kill of the CLI never leaves `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` edited in the worktree — or,
if it does, the very next invocation (or a documented one-line command) restores it exactly.

## Problem
`executeTune()` applies the edit through `applyCsvEditFile()` and restores it in a `finally`
via `restoreCsvFile()` using the in-memory `attempt.originalText`. A SIGKILL runs no `finally`,
so the edited CSV survives the process (observed on 2026-10-21 immediately after the exit-137
kill, parent item AH-0MVIKLOOJ0058Z9B).

## Expected behaviour
- Before the first edited byte is written, a small journal (target path + original bytes) is
  persisted beside the CSV and fsynced.
- The journal is git-ignored, so a crashed run never shows up as a worktree change.
- After a successful restore (or with `--keep-edit`) the journal is removed.
- Any subsequent `scripts/evaluate.mjs --tune` invocation that finds a stale journal first
  reconciles it (restores the original bytes, removes the journal, prints a warning) and then
  proceeds — so no manual step is needed in the normal case.
- A documented manual repair path exists for the case where the CSV must be restored without
  running the CLI again.

## Implementation sketch (smallest end-to-end slice)
1. New module `scripts/csvEditJournal.mjs`:
   `writeJournal(csvPath, originalBytes)` — write `<csvPath>.tune-journal` (JSON: csvPath,
   base64 original, pid, ISO timestamp) to a temp name, `fsync`, `rename` (atomic);
   `readJournal(path)`; `clearJournal(path)`; `reconcileJournal(path)` — restore original
   bytes when the journal exists, then delete it, returning `{action: 'restored'|'none'}`.
2. Wire into `executeTune()`: write the journal before `applyCsvEditFile`'s write, and clear
   it inside the existing `finally` after `restoreCsvFile()` resolves.
3. `main()` reconciles a stale journal for the `--tune` target before validation proceeds.
4. Add the journal pattern to `.gitignore` (e.g. `src/data/*.tune-journal`).
5. Document the guarantee + repair commands in `docs/BALANCING.md` (§Tuning loop →
   "Guards and guarantees"), and assert it in `src/ai/eval/balancingDocs.test.ts`.

## Key Files
- scripts/evaluate.mjs
- scripts/csvEditJournal.mjs
- scripts/evaluate-failfast.test.ts
- scripts/csvEdit-shell.test.ts
- src/utils/csvEdit.ts
- docs/BALANCING.md
- scripts/evaluate-args.test.ts

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A simulated hard kill (SIGKILL) after the edit leaves a journal; the next invocation restores the CSV byte-identical to the pre-run state, verified by a test that kills a child process and compares bytes.
2. The journal is written (fsynced, atomically renamed) beside the CSV before the edited bytes are written, and is removed after a successful restore or when --keep-edit is used.

# Per-run progress output and opt-in sweep watchdog

## Goal (user story)
As a developer (or an agent) running a long tune sweep I want visible per-run progress and an
opt-in bounded-runtime guard, so an abnormal run can never stall silently for hours and so a
timeout aborts cleanly with the CSV already restored.

## Problem
`--tune` prints nothing between start and the final summary: `executeTune()` runs two
`runBalanceBatch()` sweeps with no output. When the 2026-10-21 negative probe stalled, the only
signal was a silent process for 166.6 minutes until an external SIGKILL (parent item
AH-0MVIKLOOJ0058Z9B). After slice 2 the known hang is gone, but a future stall in the sweep
itself (configuration-driven blow-up, non-determinism guard loop, I/O stall) would again be
invisible.

## Expected behaviour
- Every `--tune` run writes one progress line per completed game to **stderr**:
  `[tune] baseline 1/2 seed=1 policy=competent`, then `[tune] candidate 2/2 …`, then the phase
  transitions (edit applied, comparing, restoring). Stdout stays byte-identical to today so
  artifact/print parity and determinism are preserved.
- `--watchdog <seconds>` (default `0` = off) arms a bounded-runtime guard: on expiry the run
  prints a diagnostic naming the phase and the elapsed time, restores the CSV (journal from
  slice 3 + synchronous restore), and exits with a distinct code (124) rather than leaving a
  killed-but-dirty worktree.
- `--help` and `docs/BALANCING.md` document both.

## Implementation sketch (smallest end-to-end slice)
1. Reuse the existing per-run hook instead of adding a second mechanism: `runBatch` already
   accepts `config.onRun` (`src/ai/eval/engine.ts`), but `runBalanceBatch()` in
   `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` does not expose it (and `CliOptions.telemetrySink` is ignored there).
   Add an optional second parameter `runBalanceBatch(options, hooks?: {onRun?})` that forwards
   `onRun`; keep the existing signature/behaviour when `hooks` is omitted.
2. In `executeTune()`, pass an `onRun` that writes the progress line to `io.err` (count games
   against `sweep.seeds.length * policies.length`) — no divergent copy of the sweep logic.
3. Add `--watchdog <seconds>` parsing to `parseEvaluateArgs` (validated: finite, >= 0;
   non-numeric → usage error exit 2), arm a timer in `executeTune()` and clear it in the
   existing `finally`; on expiry: diagnostic + `restoreCsvFile` + `process.exitCode = 124`
   (use `exitCode`, not `exit()`, so pending stderr drains and the pipe cannot mask the exit).
4. Docs: `docs/BALANCING.md` tune flags table + "Guards and guarantees"; assert in
   `src/ai/eval/balancingDocs.test.ts`.

## Risky assumptions
- A watchdog timer inside a synchronous sweep cannot interrupt a *blocking* synchronous call —
  it only fires between runs. Recorded as an accepted limitation: the guard catches stalls that
  yield to the event loop (the observed case is caught by slice 2's fail-fast path instead), and
  the progress lines remain the primary signal for a truly blocking stall. Document this
  limitation in `docs/BALANCING.md`.

## Key Files
- scripts/evaluate.mjs
- src/ai/eval/cli.ts
- src/ai/eval/engine.ts
- src/ai/eval/cli.test.ts
- scripts/evaluate-args.test.ts
- docs/BALANCING.md

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Every --tune run emits per-run progress lines on stderr (never stdout), covered by a unit test that captures both streams.
2. An opt-in bounded-runtime watchdog (--watchdog <seconds>) aborts the sweep with a clear diagnostic naming the stalled phase, restores the CSV, and exits with a distinct non-zero code, covered by a test.
3. The full verification command used in AH-0MVBNLM2V008XC8T (including the negative probe) completes without hanging, with elapsed times recorded in a work-item comment.
4. Progress wiring reuses the shared runBatch onRun hook through runBalanceBatch (no divergent sweep copy in the shell), covered by cli.test.ts.
5. Artifact/print parity is preserved: stdout and the four tune artifacts are byte-identical to the pre-change output for the same seed/options (determinism tests stay green).
6. --help and docs/BALANCING.md document --watchdog, its default (off), its exit code, and the accepted limitation that a blocking synchronous stall cannot be interrupted, asserted by the docs guard.

## Goal

As a player I want an unmistakable hyperspace "warp" when the background changes between levels, and as a developer I want that effect to be a deterministic, time-boxed, individually switchable module with a testable timeline, so level changes read as a jump through space without ever hurting readability or blocking play.

## Background

Producer answer Q2 (2026-10-25): **Option A — hyperspace-style one-shot** (converging streak overlay + radial scale distortion + brief flash/crossfade), timed to `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` (1.5 s, currently exported from `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`). Existing VFX modules show the house pattern to copy: exported tuning constants plus per-layer `*_ENABLE_*` toggles and caller-owned effect registries that are destroyed on `SHUTDOWN` (`src/vfx/endOfRunJuice.ts`, `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts`, `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts`).

Import direction matters: `PlayScene` imports VFX modules, so a VFX module must **not** import `PlayScene`. The duration therefore moves to `src/core/constants.ts` and is re-exported from `PlayScene` for existing importers.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` moves to `src/core/constants.ts` and `PlayScene` re-exports it unchanged, so `src/vfx/backgroundWarp.ts` can derive `BACKGROUND_WARP_DURATION_SECONDS` from the same single source (no duplicated literal); all existing importers (`PlayScene.test.ts`, `SceneNavigation.test.ts`) keep compiling without edits.
2. `src/vfx/backgroundWarp.ts` exposes the full timeline as exported constants (streak phase, distortion/scale phase, flash/crossfade phase) whose phases are ordered, non-overlapping and sum to the total duration; a test asserts the sum and ordering so the effect can never outlive the transition window.
3. The effect renders three layers — converging streak overlay, radial scale distortion, brief flash/crossfade into the incoming background — each with its own `BACKGROUND_WARP_ENABLE_*` toggle (following the `ENDOFRUN_ENABLE_*` pattern) and exported magnitudes (streak count, speed, colours, scale range, flash alpha).
4. Deterministic: no `Math.random()` (or a seeded generator) — two runs from the same inputs produce byte-identical layer parameters, asserted by test. Time-boxed and observable: an `update(dt)`-style tick API (no reliance on wall-clock tweens) so a test can advance exactly `BACKGROUND_WARP_DURATION_SECONDS` and assert completion; `isComplete()` is true at the end and never before.
5. Bounded and disposable: a fixed maximum streak count (constant), all display objects inside one container, `destroy()` idempotent, and a test asserts the container/children are gone after completion and after an early `destroy()` (no leaks if the scene restarts mid-warp).
6. `src/vfx/backgroundWarp.test.ts` covers the ACs above; changed-scope tests and `tsc --noEmit` pass.

**Parent:** AH-0MVIB7PD50029ZY1 — Background scenes (covers parent AC2 "changes exactly on level change", AC3 warp timing/does-not-block, AC6 integration tests).

## Goal

As a player I want the new level's background to arrive with the warp exactly when the level changes (and never mid-level), so each of the ten levels is unmistakably a different place in space while gameplay, input and wave timing are untouched.

## Background

Level changes flow `WaveManager.onEnemyDestroyed()` → `'levelCleared'` → `PlayScene._handleWaveEvent` → `_announceLevel()` + `_startTransition()` (`LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS = 1.5`). Two facts shape this slice:

1. **Two handlers.** The `levelCleared` case is duplicated in `PlayScene._handleWaveEvent` and in `PlayScene._advanceAfterTimeout()` (the wave-timer expiry path). Both must reach the background swap, so the `levelCleared` work is extracted into one helper (e.g. `_onLevelCleared()`) that both call — otherwise a level cleared by timeout skips the swap.
2. **Level is already advanced.** `WaveManager` increments `_levelIndex` *before* returning `'levelCleared'`, so `waveManager.level` during the transition is the **incoming** level: the swap target is `backgroundForLevel(waveManager.level)`, and the warp must finish no later than `transitionTimer` reaches 0 (`_onTransitionComplete()` then spawns the new wave).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. On `'levelCleared'` only — not on `'waveCleared'`, not on `'bossTriggered'`, not per wave — `PlayScene` starts the warp and swaps to `backgroundForLevel(waveManager.level)`; the same code path is reached by both the kill path (`_handleWaveEvent`) and the wave-timeout path (`_advanceAfterTimeout`), with no duplicated background logic between them.
2. The warp is created at `_startTransition()` time for a level change, advanced from the scene's own tick (not wall-clock tweens), and is complete by the time the transition ends: after ticking `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` the background's `textureKey()` equals `backgroundForLevel(newLevel)`, `isComplete()` is true, and `_onTransitionComplete()` has spawned the wave on the unchanged frame schedule.
3. Non-blocking: during the warp the player still moves, auto-fires and can teleport, and the transition/wave timer schedule is unchanged — asserted by a test that ticks half the transition while driving input and checks bullets/position, plus an assertion that `transitionRemaining()` is unaffected by the warp's presence.
4. Boss entry keeps the final level's background (documented decision: no swap and no warp on `'bossTriggered'`); asserted by test so the boss arena's backdrop is deterministic.
5. Restart/shutdown safety: starting a new run or shutting the scene down mid-warp leaves no warp container, no stale background and no leaked timer — a subsequent level change behaves normally (tested).
6. New integration suite `src/scenes/PlayScene.background.test.ts` covers ACs 1–5 and the existing `PlayScene` suites (`PlayScene.test.ts`, `PlaySceneHUD.test.ts`, `SceneNavigation.test.ts`, `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) still pass unchanged; full-suite gate is left to the dev-push gate (no ad-hoc full runs).

7. **Parent-AC traceability:** this slice's primary implementation is parent AC #6 — "Tests cover: deterministic level→background mapping, swap fires on level change (not wave), warp effect activates during the transition and completes within its duration, and the background layer does not intercept input; document updates (README, code comments, credits/attribution file with licences, GDD §3.2/§7.1 references as needed); the full project test suite passes with the new changes." — specifically the integration-tests half (swap-on-level-change-only, timing, input non-blocking, full suite); the documentation half is AH-0MVSEC4RS003KQGV; the remaining ACs of this slice are the verification and the collateral work it needs.

## Summary

Rework `PlayScene.openMiniBossReward` / `selectMiniBossReward` so a mini-boss
defeat launches the wheel overlay with the owned permanent kinds, applies the
resolved outcome exactly once through the shared reward machinery, falls back
to the hold-full-style three-option choice when nothing permanent is owned,
and keeps the demo auto-spin. The unlock machinery is already removed (parent
AC5, sibling item).

## Design

- Open: build the owned-kind snapshot once from
  `resolvePlayerSlotState(this.player).ownedIds`
  (power-up kinds and weapon drops; permanent view). When empty →
  **fallback**: open the shared `MineralChoiceScene` with the hold-full-style
  three options (`createRandomChoiceStrategy` / `chooseOptions`), applied
  permanently — a mini-boss always pays out (AC4).
- When populated: resolve the wheel outcome once from the run-seeded RNG
  (`drawWheelOutcome`/`miniBossWheel`) and launch `MiniBossWheelScene` with the
  wedges, the outcome and a single result callback. Pause exactly like the
  hold-full choice; pass the frozen fire schedule for the reduced-volume ghost
  fire; rebase the beat clock on resume.
- Select/result: apply the outcome once via `applyWheelOutcome`
  (shared reward seam), close the overlay, resume play, reset the open flag —
  a repeated select is a no-op.
- Demo mode: pass `autoSpinMs: BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS` so the attract bot
  auto-spins from the run-seeded RNG and never stalls.
- Test getters (`getMiniBossRewardOptions`, `isMiniBossRewardOpen`) preserved
  or re-homed so the wheel-flow tests keep a stable surface.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` (rework `openMiniBossReward` /
  `selectMiniBossReward`; drop unlock state)
- `src/scenes/MiniBossWheelScene.ts` (launched overlay)
- `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts` (outcome resolution + application)
- `src/powerups/slots.ts` (`resolvePlayerSlotState` — owned kinds)
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` (`chooseOptions` for the fallback)

  distribution and outcome resolver" and "Remove the weapon-unlock reward
